learningObjective: Explain the mechanism of speculative decoding and its correctness property.

canonicalClaims.claim: Speculative decoding proposes k tokens with a small draft model, verifies them in one target-model forward pass, and uses rejection sampling to accept a prefix; the retained output distribution is exactly the target's sampling distribution.
nonImplications: Does not imply arbitrary speedup; depends on acceptance rate.
Does not imply the draft model's raw outputs reach the user.

misconceptions.claim: Speculative decoding accepts the entire k-token proposal or rejects all of them via a joint-probability threshold.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Acceptance is per-token via rejection sampling on marginals; prefix length is variable.

misconceptions.claim: Speculative decoding is a form of quantization.
misconceptions.whyWrong: It is a decoding-time algorithm; unrelated to numerical precision.

misconceptions.claim: Speculative decoding requires the target and draft models to have the same weights up to scaling.
misconceptions.whyWrong: They can be entirely different architectures/checkpoints so long as vocab and tokenization match.

implementationFacts: EAGLE / Medusa / Lookahead are variants that use hidden-state prediction or n-gram heads as the draft.
Typical draft-to-target speedup is 1.5-3x on greedy or low-temperature sampling.
performanceScenarios: Higher acceptance rate (better draft-target alignment) gives more speedup.
Cold or hard prompts where the draft mispredicts often yield modest gains.
